LESSON PLAN CRE ACTIVITES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE AS A GUIDE IN OUR DAILY LIVES
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to identify reasons for reading the bible to strengthen their faith in
God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 Why should we read the bible?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Critical thinking  Responsibility Self-awareness
  Problem solving  Respect Self-esteem
  self-awareness Critical thinking
  Friendship formation citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Bible.
C.R.E activities Learner’s Book Grade 2 pg. 28-32.
C.R.E Activities Teacher’s Guide Grade 2 pg19-22.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song about the bible.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Explain to the learners the significance of the Bible as a word of God.
 Step 2: Guide learners in understanding why they should read the bible every day.
 Step 3: Learners to recite Psalms 119:105.
SUMMARY
Review the lesson and make summary.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to recite Psalms 119:105.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
With the help of the parents, learners to keep record of number of times they read the bible as a family.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: THE DIVISION OF THE BIBLE
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to identify the first two books in the Old Testament and appreciate
the bible as the word of God by reading it always.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 What are the first two books of the bible?

  Problem solving  Respect Self-esteem

  Friendship formation citizenship

Bible.
Flash cards.
C.R.E activities Learner’s Book Grade 2 pg. 33-36.
C.R.E Activities Teacher’s Guide Grade 2 pg. 20-22.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song about the bible.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide learners to understand and know that the bible has 66 books and that God is the primary author.
 Step 2: Guide learners in understanding the bible is divided into two parts (old and new testament).

 Step 4: Learners to sing a common psalm song and read their bibles.

Review the lesson and make summary.

Learners to recite Psalms 100:4.

Learners to visit a church leader for guidance on the number of books in the Old Testament.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: THE CALL OF SAMUEL
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to describe the call of Samuel and relate it to their lives by obeying
God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 What do you do when God calls you?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Critical thinking  Responsibility Self-awareness
  Problem solving  Respect Self-esteem
  self-awareness Critical thinking
  Friendship formation citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Bible.
C.R.E activities Learner’s Book Grade 2 pg. 37-41.
C.R.E Activities Teacher’s Guide Grade 2 pg. 22-24.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song on the call of Samuel.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide learners to read the Bible story of the call of Samuel from 1Samuel 3:3-11.
 Step 2: Guide learners in watching a video with the story of the call of Samuel.
 Step 3: Learners to role play the call of Samuel.
SUMMARY
Review the lesson.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to recite 1 Samuel 3:3-11.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to visit a church and listen to the Bible story on the call of Samuel.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE HOLY BIBLE
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: NOAH AND THE ARK
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to state the reason why God chose Noah to build the ark and live a
life that is pleasing to God.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 Why should we obey God?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Critical thinking  Responsibility Self-awareness
  Problem solving  Respect Self-esteem
  self-awareness  Obedience Critical thinking
  Decision making  Care and love citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Bible.
Video clips.
C.R.E activities Learner’s Book Grade 2 pg. 42-49.
C.R.E Activities Teacher’s Guide Grade 2 pg. 25-28.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song on Noah and the Ark.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Explain to the learners on the importance of being obedient and od-fearing in relation to the Biblical
 account of Noah.
 Step 2: Guide learners in watching a video with the story of Noah and the Ark.
 Step 3: Learners to role play in small groups the story of Noah and the Ark.
SUMMARY
Noah and his family built the ark.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to Read Genesis 6:9-10
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to visit a church elder and listen to the Bible story of Noah and the Ark.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: THE STORY OF DANIEL
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to acquire the skill of assertiveness by emulating Daniel in their lives
and appreciate God as the protector by trusting him.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 Why is the importance of being courageous?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Critical thinking  Faith Self-awareness
  Problem solving  Patience Self-esteem
  self-awareness  Courage and trust Critical thinking
  Decision making citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Bible.
Video clips
C.R.E activities Learner’s Book Grade 2 pg. 50-56.
C.R.E Activities Teacher’s Guide Grade 2 pg. 29-31.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song on about Daniel.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Learners to Read the story of Daniel in the lion’s Den in Daniel 6:10-12, 19-22.
 Step 2: Learners to watch a video on the story of Daniel in the Den of Lions.
 Step 3: Learners to role play Daniel in the Den of lions and how he was rescued.
 Step 4: Learners to discuss how to be assertive in life.
SUMMARY
We should be bold each time.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to recite Daniel 6:10-12
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to participate in church activities that will strengthen their trust in God.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON/SELF-REMARKS
